newsitem.title: USA: IMM CURRENCY FUTURES MIXED, SEPT STERLING SLIDES.
newsitem.headline: IMM CURRENCY FUTURES MIXED, SEPT STERLING SLIDES.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mixed early as recent laggards firmed but sterling slumped.
September marks and Swiss edged up slightly from Wednesday's new contract lows, and yen also showed mild resilience.
September sterling, meanwhile, fell through $1.58 support.
"Sterling is the big story," an IMM curreny analyst said. The Bank of England raised interest rates a quarter-point, but the move was widely seen as the last for some time.
Players were aggressively buying marks and selling sterling after the rate hike, traders said.
"I really don't think the mark is very strong, it's just a function of sterling," the analyst said.

The BOE's monetary policy committee early Thursday raised official rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent, as many had expected. But they also said that rates were now consistent with their inflation target.
The currency analyst said gains in marks and Swiss were negligible in the overall picture. Others said the contracts would likely continue their series of contract lows.
Resistance in marks was pegged at $0.5353 to $0.5362 and at $0.6583 in Swiss francs.
Traders said key cash levels that were pierced earlier this week now hover above the market as dollar resistance, namely 1.88 marks and 119 yen.
September yen pushed to the highest price in almost a week and remained near session highs.
Yen resistance was put at $0.008524, about 117.92 spot.

At 0829 CDT/1329 GMT, September yen was up $0.000054 at $0.008523, marks were up $0.0029 at $0.5356, Swiss francs were $0.0030 higher at $0.6584, sterling fell $0.0148 at $1.5836, Canadian dollars were off $0.0004 at $0.7222, Australian dollars were up $0.0009 at $0.7372 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000175 at $0.126850.
